title: CTV Overtakes Cable in Political Ad Spend for the First Time in a Midterm

facts.fact: Political advertisers had spent $11.4 billion to date in the 2026 midterms cycle, up 28% from the 2022 midterms, according to AdImpact data shared with ADWEEK.
facts.quote: political advertisers have spent $11.4 billion to date, up 28% from the 2022 midterms, according to data shared with ADWEEK from AdImpact

facts.fact: According to AdImpact, the 2026 midterms cycle has already drawn more ad spend than any election cycle AdImpact tracks, including the 2024 U.S. presidential cycle.
facts.quote: The cycle has already drawn more ad spend than any election cycle tracked by AdImpact

facts.fact: The 2024 U.S. presidential cycle set a previous AdImpact-tracked political ad spend record of $11.2 billion.
facts.quote: the 2024 U.S. presidential cycle, which set a previous record of $11.2 billion

facts.fact: Of the $2.5 billion increase in political ad investment from the 2022 midterms, more than half (53%) went to connected TV, per AdImpact data.
facts.quote: more than half (53%) has gone to connected TV

facts.fact: Political ad spend in connected TV grew 122%, from roughly $1.1 billion in the 2022 midterms to $2.4 billion in the 2026 cycle, per AdImpact data.
facts.quote: On the whole, spend in CTV grew 122%, from roughly $1.1 billion in the 2022 midterms to $2.4

facts.fact: Political ad spend on cable fell 26% to less than $1.3 billion compared with the 2022 cycle, per the article's data.
facts.quote: while cable fell 26% to less than $1.3 billion

facts.fact: A related Adweek headline on this page states that political campaigns spent a near-record $331 per voter in the midterms, though waste is forcing a rethink.
facts.quote: Political Campaigns Spent a Near-Record $331 Per Voter, But Waste Forces Rethink

facts.fact: A related Adweek headline on this page reports that Fox Corp. completed a $22 billion deal for Roku.
facts.quote: Fox Corp. Completes $22 Billion Deal for Roku
